outcome: Maternal and fetal outcomes of ECV
Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
cohort: 67 pregnant women who underwent successful ECV at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia Medical Centre (UKMMC) between September 2008 and September 2010
finding: While successful ECV led to a higher gestational age at delivery, it was also associated with an increased need for labor induction, a higher rate of cesarean sections and obstetric complications.
mod_finding: Women who underwent successful external cephalic version (ECV) were at higher risk of carrying the pregnancy beyond 40 weeks, needing induction of labor, and having a cesarean section compared to women with cephalic singletons.
